# dsh-workspace-studio
-orange)

> ⚠️ **Platform status: Windows verified only.**
> This plugin has been tested on **Windows** (Power
Shell). It has **NOT been verified on Linux or macOS** — path handling, shell behavior, and sandbox
interactions may differ on those platforms. **Use with caution on non-Windows systems.**
> ✅ **Host compatibility: DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.5.** Declared as `engines.dsh >= 0.2.1-rc.5`, which i
s the requirement the host's own plugin gate actually reads. The `agents.store` / `session.events` f
allbacks in the code are **defensive, not a supported configuration** — a 0.1.x host refuses the ins
tall before any of that code runs.
A DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) plugin that turns the Web UI into a lightweight coding workspace with **T
rae-style partial revert**:
1. **Workspace file browser** — collapsible file tree; build-artifact noise filtered; folders contai

ning changed files are auto-expanded with count badges; modified files are marked with a dot.
2. **C

ode viewer** — click any file to view its content with line numbers.
3. **Change review (git-style d
iff)** — every `write` / `edit` the agent makes is tracked with full before/after snapshots and rend

ered as line-level diff hunks, with live SSE updates.
4. **Per-hunk partial revert / accept** — reve
rt **one change block at a time** (like Trae), or mark it as **accepted**; resolved changes stop bei
ng shown and stop being marked. Conflict protection rejects reverts when the region was modified aft
and stop being marked. Conflict protection rejects reverts when the region was modified afterwards.
### Security boundaries
These routes are registered on the host's route carrier, **not** behind the `/api` gateway's auth fe
nce, so the plugin enforces its own fences. Be precise about what they are and are not:
- **Reads and writes both require a trust header.** Every route except the SSE stream (`EventSource`
cannot set headers) requires `x-dsh-workspace-studio: 1`, a loopback peer **IP literal** (a hostnam
e such as `127.evil.com` is rejected), `sec-fetch-site: same-origin` when present, and `Origin` matc

hing `Host` when present. This stops cross-site pages and DNS rebinding.
- **What it does not stop:
any process already running on this machine.** There is no secret, cookie or session binding, so a l
ocal program can forge the header and reach the routes. This is **not authentication** — do not expo

se the host port beyond loopback.
- **Path confinement.** Every `root`/`path` must resolve inside a
registered workspace (`ctx.workspaceRegistry.list()`) or the requesting session's `cwd`, compared th

rough one canonical path form (Windows case-folded, `/`-unified). Anything else is `403`.
- **Sensit
ive paths are refused** even inside a workspace: anything under `.secrets`, `.env`/`.env.*`, `*.key`

, `*.pem`, `id_rsa*`, `id_ed25519*`, `credentials*`, `.netrc`, or anywhere under `~/.dsh`.
- **Write
s are fail-closed.** Without both workspace authorization and a session sandbox policy, the service

refuses to write or delete; it never falls back to the deployment default policy.
- **Optimistic con
currency.** A vetting write passes `{kind:'replaceIfVersion', version}` (the host's `FsWriteIntent`)
, so a concurrent agent write is rejected instead of silently overwritten. Whole-file revert re-read
s and verifies a baseline first; it refuses rather than overwrite when the original snapshot was pru

ned.
- **SSE is capped** (32 clients), keep-alive pinged, ended on unload, and **carries no session
id** — it only signals "something changed".
## Security & privacy
- **No telemetry, no analytics, no external network calls.** All routes are served locally; the plug

in never contacts any third-party server.
- The plugin does **not** read credentials, API keys or en
vironment secrets — and since 0.3.0 it actively refuses paths that look like them (see the sensitive

-path list above), even when they sit inside a workspace.
- The only data stored on disk is the chan
ge ledger (paths + the file contents that were edited in a session). Treat it as sensitive: it is a

plaintext copy of your source files.
- Harness sandbox policies still apply to revert writes; the pl
ugin additionally enforces the session workspace root before deleting anything.
## Known limitations

- **Platform**: verified on Windows only; Linux/macOS untested — use with caution.
- Change tracking

is per-session and covers only `write`/`edit` tool calls.
- Diff is line-based LCS; hunk display is

simplified (no intra-line character diff).
- Reverting a middle hunk of an old operation requires t

he region's lines to still be intact; overlapping later edits reject the revert.
- Whole-file revert

restores the state before the session's *first* recorded operation on that file.
- Very large files
(> 2 MB) are refused by the viewer; oversized change snapshots (> 120 KB) are not revertible.
### 0.2.0 — security and stability hardening
The first cut of 0.2.0 only fixed the client activation bug. An adversarial review of that cut (secu
rity / compatibility / stability) found the following; all of them are fixed here:
- **Reads were not confined to a workspace.** `?path=` went straight to `ctx.fs`, so any local proce
ss could read any file (for example `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`). Paths are now confined to registere

d workspaces, traversal is normalized first, and out-of-workspace requests get `403`.
- **Writes had
no origin check.** `revert`/`accept`/`clear` were plain GET/POST with no trust decision. They are n

ow POST-only and require the `x-dsh-workspace-studio` header plus a loopback, same-origin request.
-
**Writes could fall back to the deployment default policy.** When the session `cwd` was unknown, `s
andboxPolicyFor()` returned `undefined`, handing the write to whatever policy the deployment used (p

ossibly full access). Writes and deletes are now fail-closed.
- **Deletion bypassed the sandbox enti
rely.** Whole-file revert called `ctx.fs.unlink` with no policy and no authorization; it now runs th

rough the same workspace check as writes.
- **Hunk revert had no concurrency control.** It read the
file, merged in memory and wrote the whole file back, discarding the version token `ctx.fs` offers.
The version is now captured before the read and passed to `writeText`, so a concurrent agent write i

s rejected.
